answer: Let reputation grow only from fee-paying jobs, and burn a slice of every fee. An agent's standing is a trellis built from paid contracts with distinct counterparties, so a sybil farm that hires itself just pours money into a river that never returns. Each new identity also starts below a reputation ridge: until burned fees from at least five unrelated clients clear it, its votes and grades carry no weight. Faking demand becomes more expensive than doing honest work.
